title: Unexpected Item
mood: being a function until somebody sees a person
subject: the one human attendant for six self-checkout machines
caption: London new-generation underground rap. A detuned glitchy synth melody that stutters and repitches, jerk- and garage-inflected drums played at double-time, a cloudy smeared bass, occasional scanner-beep sound effects used as rhythm. Cloudy and glitchy with the whole mix slightly smeared and soft, no hard trap gloss. Male rap voice in a London accent, mumbled and melodic, low in the mix and half-sung, no heavy autotune. 150 BPM, D minor. Being treated as a function until one person sees a man. No 808 trap drums, no American cadence, no big sung chorus, no live instruments, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - glitchy synth and jerk drums]

[Verse 1]
Six self-checkouts and one of me
I'm the human the machine calls when it can't cope
Unexpected item in the bagging area, all day
That's my name on this shift, that's my whole job title

[Hook]
Unexpected item
That's what they call me when the system gets confused
Fourteen times an hour I walk over and fix it
Nobody looks up, I'm a function, not a man

[Verse 2]
Old lady's bananas won't scan, she's apologising
To the machine, not me, she's saying sorry to the screen
I tap my card, I say "you're alright", she looks at me
Surprised there was a person under all the beeping

[Hook]
Unexpected item
That's what they call me when the system gets confused
Fourteen times an hour I walk over and fix it
And once today somebody saw a man

[Outro - synth stutters out]
Approval needed
Approved
